0.text: XVIII. — ORGANIZATION OF FAMILY AND FAMILY-GROUP.

1.text: MAN IN THE FAMILY. — The units of social organization among the

2.text: Chukchee are quite unstable, excepting the family, which forms the basis of

3.text: the social relations between members of the tribe. Even family ties are not

4.text: absolutely binding, and single persons often break them and leave their family

5.text: relations. Grown-up sons frequently leave their parents and go away to

6.text: distant localities in search of a fortune. The youths of the Reindeer tribe

7.text: descend to the coast, and those of the Maritime Chukchee go inland to live

8.text: with the reindeer-breeders. Not a few of the Chukchee tales open with a

9.text: description of the life of a lone man who does not know any other people,

10.text: and who lives in a wild place. It may be said that a lone man living by

11.text: himself forms the real unit of Chukchee society. Even woman, whose social

12.text: position is much inferior to that of man, sometimes breaks away from father

13.text: or husband and goes to live with other people, though the family may pursue

14.text: her, and, if she is caught, bring her back by force. Such cases will be

16.text: I do not know of any cases of this kind happening among the Tungus,

17.text: where the family and clan organization are much stronger. Tungus families
